newsitem.title: USA: Exxon upstream operations aid Q3 profits.
newsitem.headline: Exxon upstream operations aid Q3 profits.

text.p: Exxon Corp said on Monday that higher oil and natural gas prices and a 65 percent increase in exploration and production results led to record net income for a third quarter.

"Exxon achieved record net income for a third quarter as a result of increased natural gas, petroleum product and chemical sales, as well as stronger crude oil and natural gas prices," Exxon chairman Lee Raymond said in a statement.
"Earnings for the first nine months of 1996 are also the highest in Exxon's history," he said.

Exxon's third quarter net income of $1.56 billion topped the previous third quarter record of $1.50 billion a year ago. Exxon's overall record for quarterly earnings was $2.24 billion in the first quarter of 1991.
Typically the first and fourth quarters are strongest due to winter demand for natural gas and heating oil worldwide, an Exxon spokesman said.
Worldwide crude oil prices averaged about $4.50 a barrel more than last year and higher natural gas prices helped increase gas sales by 8 percent in the third quarter over a year ago, Exxon said.

Exxon's U.S. exploration and production earnings, which are known as upstream operations, increased to $395 million in the third quarter from $209 million a year ago. International upstream operations for the third quarter increased to $583 million from $385 million a year ago.
Refining and marketing earnings declined from last year's third quarter as industry margins remained under pressure, Exxon said.
Chemical operations achieved record third quarter sales, but earnings were below last year's third quarter due to lower chemical prices and higher feedstock costs, Exxon said.
